title: Structured validation of syndromic surveillance alerts: a day-randomised comparison in a regional public health agency
abstract: Objective: to test whether a structured validation checklist shortens the time from syndromic surveillance alert to validation decision without increasing dismissed true events. Design: randomised comparison with duty days allocated to the checklist or usual validation, January to June 2027. Primary outcome: time to validation decision. Results and conclusions will be written after the evaluation.
introduction: Syndromic surveillance generates many alerts, few of them real, and validation practice varies widely. Accuracy studies of validation procedures depend on panel review, which hindsight biases.
methods: Duty days were randomised in blocks within month. Time stamps came from the surveillance log, and outbreak reports classified alerts. A mixed model compared log times; a safety panel reviewed every dismissed true event.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present alert flow, times by procedure, escalations, contamination and each dismissed true event.
discussion: The discussion will weigh time saved against dismissed events and state whether the checklist should become standard.
limitations: One agency; six epidemiologists; few true events.
conclusion: To be written after the evaluation; it will not claim a change in outbreak detection rates.
reportingChecklist: CONSORT extension for cluster randomised trials
summary: CONSORT-structured draft with results left empty.
